sentences.text: Buddhism -LRB- -LSB- pronˈbʊdɪzəm -RSB- or -LSB- ˈbuːdɪzəm -RSB- -RRB- is an Indian religion and dharma that encompasses a variety of traditions , beliefs and spiritual practices largely based on teachings attributed to the Buddha .	Indian religion	Indian religions	dharma	dharma	teachings	Original Teachings of the Buddha	the Buddha	Gautama Buddha	Buddha	Gautama Buddha

Buddhism originated in Ancient India sometime between the 6th and 4th centuries BCE , from where it spread through much of Asia , whereafter it declined in India during the middle ages .	Ancient India	Ancient India	Asia	Asia	declined in India	Decline of Buddhism in India

Two major extant branches of Buddhism are generally recognized by scholars : Theravada -LRB- Pali : `` The School of the Elders '' -RRB- and Mahayana -LRB- Sanskrit : `` The Great Vehicle '' -RRB- .	Theravada	Theravada	Pali	Pali	Mahayana	Mahayana	Sanskrit	Sanskrit
Buddhism is the world 's fourth-largest religion , with over 500 million followers or 7 % of the global population , known as Buddhists .

Buddhist schools vary on the exact nature of the path to liberation , the importance and canonicity of various teachings and scriptures , and especially their respective practices .	teachings	Original Teachings of the Buddha	Buddhist schools	Schools of Buddhism	canonicity of various teachings and scriptures	Buddhist texts	scriptures	Buddhist texts

Practices of Buddhism include taking refuge in the Buddha , the Dharma and the Sangha , study of scriptures , observance of moral precepts , renunciation of craving and attachment , the practice of meditation -LRB- including calm and insight -RRB- , the cultivation of wisdom , loving-kindness and compassion , the Mahayana practice of bodhicitta and the Vajrayana practices of generation stage and completion stage .	the Buddha	Gautama Buddha	Mahayana	Mahayana	refuge	Refuge (Buddhism)	Buddha	Gautama Buddha	Dharma	Dharma#Buddhism	Sangha	Sangha	scriptures	Buddhist texts	moral precepts	Buddhist ethics	renunciation	Nekkhamma	craving	Taṇhā	attachment	Upādāna	meditation	Buddhist meditation	calm	samatha	insight	vipassanā	wisdom	Prajñā (Buddhism)	loving-kindness	Mettā	compassion	Karuṇā	bodhicitta	bodhicitta	generation stage	generation stage	completion stage	completion stage	Vajrayana	Vajrayana

In Theravada the ultimate goal is the cessation of the kleshas and the attainment of the sublime state of Nirvana , achieved by practicing the Noble Eightfold Path -LRB- also known as the Middle Way -RRB- , thus escaping what is seen as a cycle of suffering and rebirth .	Theravada	Theravada	kleshas	Kleshas (Buddhism)	Nirvana	Nirvana (Buddhism)	Noble Eightfold Path	Noble Eightfold Path	Middle Way	Middle Way	cycle	Saṃsāra (Buddhism)	suffering	Dukkha	rebirth	Rebirth (Buddhism)
Theravada has a widespread following in Sri Lanka and Southeast Asia .	Asia	Asia	Theravada	Theravada	Sri Lanka	Buddhism in Sri Lanka	Southeast Asia	Buddhism in Southeast Asia

Mahayana , which includes the traditions of Pure Land , Zen , Nichiren Buddhism , Shingon and Tiantai -LRB- Tendai -RRB- , is found throughout East Asia . Rather than Nirvana , Mahayana instead aspires to Buddhahood via the bodhisattva path , a state wherein one remains in the cycle of rebirth to help other beings reach awakening . Vajrayana , a body of teachings attributed to Indian siddhas , may be viewed as a third branch or merely a part of Mahayana .	teachings	Original Teachings of the Buddha	Mahayana	Mahayana	Vajrayana	Vajrayana	Indian siddhas	mahasiddha
